criteria_quotes: Rotator cuff repair is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met: • MRI or CT shows EITHER of the following findings: ◦ Grade 2 or 3 partial-thickness rotator cuff tear (Ellman classification) ◦ full-thickness rotator cuff tear (Cofield classification)

Classification of rotator cuff tears (based upon surgical findings): • Partial-thickness tears, also called incomplete tears (Ellman): ◦ Grade 1: <3mm deep (<25% thickness) ◦ Grade 2: 3–6mm in depth but not exceeding 50% of the tendon thickness ◦ Grade 3: >6mm deep (>50% thickness) • Full-thickness tears, also called complete tears (Cofield): ◦ Small: <1cm ◦ Medium: 1-3cm ◦ Large: 3-5cm ◦ Massive: >5cm
answer.submission_route:

1. ONLINE: Providers can submit appeals electronically via CignaForHCP.com or Provider.Evernorth.com.
2. BY MAIL: For clinical appeals managed by EviCore (which administers musculoskeletal procedures for Cigna), mail the appeal packet to: EviCore Claim Appeals, P.O. Box 5620, Hartford, CT 06102. Alternatively, standard Cigna Network appeals can be mailed to: Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8011 (or P.O. 3. BY FAX: Send to the plan-specific fax number printed on the original denial letter.
4. BY PHONE: Contact Cigna Customer Service at 1-800-882-4462 to review the decision. To schedule an EviCore clinical discussion or peer-to-peer review, call EviCore directly at 1-866-668-9250 within 30 days of the denial.
